Title: Batu Kawan's MKH Oil Palm offer closes at 79.58pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Kawan Bhd's mandatory take-over offer for the remaining voting shares in MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd has closed, with the offeror and parties acting in concert holding 79.58 per cent.
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd, acting for offeror Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd and ultimate offeror Batu Kawan, said the offer closed at 5pm on Thursday.
The cash offer was priced at RM0.6626 per share.
The mandatory offer stemmed from Batu Kawan's acquisition of a controlling stake in MKH Bhd, which also triggered the obligation to extend an offer for MKH Oil Palm shares.
In May, Whitmore agreed to acquire stakes in MKH and MKH Oil Palm from the Chen family and related parties.
The transactions included a 3.9 per cent direct stake in MKH Oil Palm, while MKH and its subsidiaries collectively held a substantial interest in the plantation company.
Following completion of the MKH acquisition, Whitmore became obliged to make the unconditional mandatory offer for MKH Oil Palm at RM0.6626 per share.
The offer document was posted on Aug 27, with the acceptance period running until Sept 17.
As at the closing date, Whitmore, Batu Kawan and persons acting in concert held 701.9 million MKH Oil Palm shares, or 69.20 per cent as at Aug 27, the posting date of the offer document.
They received valid acceptances for an additional 99.07 million shares, representing 9.77 per cent , while acquiring or agreeing to acquire a further 6.19 million shares, or 0.61 per cent , outside the acceptance process.
This brought their total holdings to 807.16 million shares, or 79.58 per cent, based on 1.014 billion MKH Oil Palm shares in issue, excluding treasury shares.
A further 88,647 shares, equivalent to 0.01 per cent, were subject to verification.

Title: Johor stray dog catcher suspended after video sparks backlash
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A municipal stray dog catcher has been suspended after a video allegedly showing him making an obscene hand gesture at members of the public during an operation went viral yesterday.
Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the action was unacceptable.
He said the worker was suspended pending an investigation, while the contractor and representatives of an animal welfare association were called to assist in the probe.
Ling said stray animal-catching operations would be monitored to ensure they were carried out professionally.
The video showed workers wearing Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) vests catching a stray dog while a person in a car filmed the operation and confronted them over how it was being handled.
One of the workers responded with an obscene hand gesture.
The footage sparked a social media backlash, with users alleging that the dog catchers had handled the dogs in an inhumane manner and condemning the worker's aggressive behaviour towards the resident.
Meanwhile, MPBP said in a statement that the incident involved an appointed stray animal management contractor.
The council said it would call the contractor and representatives of the animal welfare association to obtain a full explanation.
It also said the contractor would be directed to take firm action against the worker if misconduct was established.
MPBP said it would strengthen monitoring and make improvements to prevent a recurrence, while urging all parties to cooperate in addressing stray animal issues and prioritise public safety.

Title: [UPDATED] Najib's special officer arrives at Langgak Duta residence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A special officer to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was seen arriving at his Langgak Duta residence this evening, hours after he was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Ahmad Lutfi Azhar was seen entering the compound in a black Proton sport utility vehicle (SUV) at about 4.35pm.
His arrival marked one of the first movements observed at the residence, where more than 50 local and international media personnel as well as supporterd have been stationed since earlier today following the announcement of the conditional pardon.
Among them was Siti Suzzalina Anuar, 43, who travelled from Lenggeng, Negri Sembilan, to show her support for Najib.
Siti Suzzalina said she had supported Najib for years and had been eagerly awaiting his release.
"I came from Lenggeng after work to show my support.
"We miss Datuk Seri Najib's leadership. I have been his supporter for a long time," she said when met outside the residence today.
Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that Najib, 73, had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under
house arrest
until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
The decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya at Istana Negara today.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
Najib must comply with all conditions imposed under the pardon, failing which it will be revoked and he will be required to immediately serve the remainder of his sentence in prison.
Najib has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and sentence in the SRC International case.
He was convicted of seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million belonging to SRC International.
Najib was originally sentenced to 12 years' jail and fined RM210 million.
In 2024, the Pardons Board reduced his jail term to six years and his fine to RM50 million, setting his release date at Aug 23, 2028.

Title: Road closures in George Town for Tanjong Lantern Festival tomorrow
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Several roads around Lebuh Armenian, Lebuh Acheh and Lorong Lumut here will be temporarily closed tomorrow in conjunction with the Tanjong Lantern Festival.
The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) said in a statement that the closure will be from noon until 11.59pm on the same day.
The affected roads are parts of Lebuh Armenian from Lebuh Acheh to Lebuh Cannon, Lebuh Acheh from Lebuh Cannon to Lebuh Carnarvon, and Lorong Lumut.
The public, especially road users, are advised to plan their journeys in advance, follow the closure instructions and use suitable alternative routes.
MBPP said public cooperation and attention were appreciated to ensure the festival proceeds smoothly and safely.

Title: MCA: Judicial, pardon processes separate under Constitution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA believes that the judicial and pardon processes should be understood as two separate processes within the framework of the Federal Constitution.
MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the party expressed its appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia for the royal pardon granted conditionally to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
"MCA believes that the judicial process and the pardon process should be understood as two separate processes within the framework of the Federal Constitution.
"Therefore, respecting the decision of the Pardons Board does not mean denying the court's decision, just as respecting the court's decision does not mean questioning the pardoning power provided for under the Constitution.
"Both are part of the country's legal and constitutional system and must be respected," he said in a statement today.
He said MCA would continue to uphold the principles of the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law as enshrined in the Rukun Negara, as well as uphold the institution of the constitutional monarchy, which is one of the country's key pillars.
"MCA will also continue to adhere to the principle that institutions must be respected, the law must be upheld and integrity must be defended," he said.
Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board said Najib had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.
The board said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had
consented to the conditional pardon.
It added that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed under the pardon, failing which the conditional pardon could be revoked.
Najib, 73, is currently serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the Pardons Board reduced his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.
The board also reduced the RM210 million fine imposed on him to RM50 million.
Najib began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and sentence in the SRC International case.
He was found guilty of seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering over RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former unit of 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).
He was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.

Title: No sign of Najib leaving Kajang Prison as of 3.30pm
Article:

granted a conditional pardon

Title: [UPDATED]: DAP CEC to meet tomorrow over Najib's conditional house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP will hold a central executive committee (CEC) meeting tomorrow to discuss and decide on the party's position and subsequent course of action.
The meeting follows the decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
In a statement, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) scandal was a major corruption scandal in the country's history and had affected Malaysia's image and public and investor confidence in government institutions.
It said Najib's conviction in the case involving 1MDB was a matter decided by the courts and its impact on the country should not be forgotten.
"The financial impact of the misconduct is still being borne by the country and the people to this day," it said.
DAP said according to a Finance Ministry statement dated Sept 13, the government's total 1MDB obligations stood at RM51.4 billion, comprising RM42.5 billion already paid by the government and RM8.9 billion in outstanding debt.
"DAP has been consistent from the outset in demanding justice and accountability over the 1MDB scandal.
"We advocated for the misconduct to be thoroughly investigated and for those responsible to be brought through an independent and fair legal process," he said.
DAP also said public anger over the 1MDB scandal was among the factors that led to a change in government at the 14th General Election in 2018.
"The people's mandate to oppose corruption and abuse of power will continue to guide DAP," he said.
On the latest development, DAP said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh had conveyed a position and views consistent with the party's principles while carrying out her responsibilities as a member of the Pardons Board.
"At the same time, DAP respects the King's pardoning powers as provided for under the Federal Constitution.
"DAP has always upheld the principles of constitutional monarchy and the supremacy of the Constitution, while defending the rule of law and its fight against corruption.
"As such, a meeting of the DAP CEC will be held tomorrow to discuss and decide on the party's position and subsequent course of action," he said.
Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board said Najib
had been granted
a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.
The board said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
It added that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed under the pardon, failing which the conditional pardon could be revoked.
Najib, 73, is currently serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the Pardons Board reduced his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.
The board also reduced the RM210 million fine imposed on him to RM50 million.
Najib began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and sentence in the SRC International case.
He was found guilty of seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering over RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former unit of 1MDB.
He was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.

Title: Police tighten security in Negri Sembilan amid royal institution developments
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Police have tightened security measures across Negri Sembilan following developments concerning the state's royal institution.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad urged all parties to remain patient and allow the relevant authorities to resolve the matter in accordance with the law.
"The role of the police is to ensure public order. When issues like this arise, we maintain heightened attention toward security across all areas," he said after performing Friday prayers at the Tuanku Munawir Royal Mosque in Seri Menanti today.
Commenting on a police report lodged by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim regarding allegations that he was forced to sign a proclamation, Alzafny said details would be disclosed at an appropriate time.
Earlier, Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir attended Friday prayers at the mosque, accompanied by his two sons, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin.
Meanwhile, security has also been stepped up at Wisma Negeri in Seremban, which houses the Negri Sembilan State Secretariat.
Visitors seeking entry to the building are required to undergo security checks and verification.
Members of the public must state their purpose of visit and the name of the officer they intend to meet before being granted access.
Media personnel are subjected to similar procedures, requiring them to state the individual they wish to meet despite presenting valid media passes.
However, it remains unconfirmed whether these measures constitute a new directive or form part of existing security protocols.
Yesterday, the Negri Sembilan State Secretariat said in a statement that it would not proceed with the gazettement or implementation of
the proclamation
to dethrone Tuanku Muhriz.
It said the decision was in line with the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) view that the proclamation was invalid, making any attempt to gazette it unconstitutional.
The office said the state government abided by the A-GC's view that members of the Negri Sembilan state executive council had no jurisdiction, authority or power under the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 to announce the proclamation.

Title: Shark kills swimmer off beach in Western Australia
Article:
SYDNEY: A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia on Friday, police said.
It was the fourth death from a shark attack in Australia this year.
"It was reported a male swimmer had been bitten by a shark while swimming along the coast," a Western Australia state police spokeswoman said in a statement.
"The swimmer died as a result of the attack."
Police helicopters and boats scoured waters off Sorrento Beach after emergency services were called to the beach in the morning, officials said.
Authorities closed beaches in the area until further notice.
Local media reported that witnesses had seen blood in the water.
"It was like a scene off Jaws where a body is flicked around like a rag doll," an unidentified male witness on the beach told local broadcaster Seven.
Surf Life Saving WA said in a social media post that an unidentified species of shark was involved in the incident about 50m offshore.
It was the second shark attack in Western Australia this week, after a man lost part of his leg when he was bitten at Glenfield Beach, north of Perth.
There have been multiple shark attack fatalities around the country this year.
A 12-year-old boy died after he was bitten by a shark while swimming in Sydney Harbour in January.
Three divers were fatally mauled in separate incidents between May and June – two in Western Australia and the third in Queensland.
Also in June, a woman had to have part of her left arm amputated after she was mauled by a shark at one of Australia's most popular beaches, Coogee, in Sydney.
There have been around 1,300 shark incidents around Australia since 1791, of which more than 260 resulted in death, according to a database of their encounters with humans.

Title: Malaysia proposes Asean Halal Council launch in September 2027
Article:
JAKARTA: Malaysia has proposed the formal establishment and launch of the Asean Halal Council in the country in September 2027 as part of efforts to turn the idea of a regional halal council into a functioning institution, according to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said Malaysia was also prepared to serve as the council's secretariat, subject to the agreement of Asean member states and partners, while proposing Indonesia as its inaugural chair.
"Malaysia and Indonesia first put forward this idea last year. Today, I believe the time has come to move from discussion to institution," he said in his keynote address at the fifth Halal 20 (H20) Summit today.
The Asean Halal Council was first proposed by Ahmad Zahid during a Malaysia-Indonesia halal industry roundtable and his meeting with Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka in Jakarta in April 2025, with both countries subsequently agreeing in May that year to jointly spearhead its formation.
Zahid, who is also chairman of the Halal Industry Development Council (MPIH), said the proposal had been submitted to the Asean Secretariat and would next be brought to the Asean Summit in Manila for endorsement.
He said Asean could not wait any longer as the halal economy was expanding rapidly and the market would not wait for the region to organise itself.
"Between now and then, we must put in place the council's mandate, governance and first deliverables so that it is ready to act from day one," he said.
He also viewed the Asean Halal Council as an important building block towards the proposed World Halal Development Council, with the discussion to be taken further at the Malaysia International Halal Showcase (MIHAS) in Kuala Lumpur later this month.
On the wider halal economy, Ahmad Zahid said Muslim consumer spending across six key sectors reached USD2.6 trillion (USD1 = RM4.09) in 2024 and is projected to grow to around USD3.56 trillion by 2029, with halal food alone accounting for more than USD1.5 trillion in spending.
"Asean is particularly well positioned to capture this growth. With more than 250 million halal consumers, we already have the scale, industries and capabilities to become a major force in the global halal economy.
"Yet our strengths are not always connected as effectively as they should be. Differences in standards, certification and accreditation continue to create friction, while businesses still face duplication and barriers across markets," he said.
He said the question was no longer whether demand existed, but whether the region was connected enough to capture that growth together.
Zahid arrived in Jakarta yesterday for a four-day working visit at the invitation of Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency in conjunction with the summit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sunway Healthcare breaks ground on RM800mil Johor hospital
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Healthcare Group has begun construction of Sunway Medical Centre Iskandar Puteri, its first hospital in Johor, with an estimated capital expenditure of RM800 million.
The hospital is targeted for completion in 2030 and will have a capacity of more than 400 beds.
The hospital will offer a comprehensive range of specialist services, supported by advanced medical technologies and patient-centred treatment facilities.
These will include an integrated cancer and nuclear medicine centre offering radiotherapy and nuclear medicine services.
Other key specialities at the hospital include cardiovascular, oncology, neuroscience, gastroenterology and hepatology, orthopaedics, as well as women and children's health.
The hospital will employ more than 1,400 healthcare professionals upon its targeted completion and will be equipped with more than 45 intensive care beds and over 130 ambulatory care beds.
It will also have more than 80 consultation suites, 10 operating theatres and two catheterisation laboratories.
Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah said Sunway has always believed in Johor's immense potential and that quality healthcare is essential to sustaining the state's growth.
"Businesses choose to invest where people can build secure and fulfilling lives, and families place their trust in places where quality medical care is within reach.
"We look forward to building a trusted medical institution that serves Johor and the wider region for generations to come," said Cheah.
Beyond SMCIP, the group is also expanding its healthcare presence in Johor.
This is through the planned Sunway Fertility Centre at Sunway Citrine, targeted for completion in 2027, and the Sunway Ambulatory Care Centre near the Johor Bahru–Singapore RTS Link, targeted for completion in 2028.
Sunway Healthcare Group president Datuk Lau Beng Long said SMCIP will be more than a standalone hospital.
As part of the integrated Sunway City Iskandar Puteri township, it will support the health and well-being of surrounding communities.
"Today's groundbreaking marks an important step towards realising our vision for Sunway Medical Centre Iskandar Puteri," said Lau.

Title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for 10 states until 5pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across 10 states until 5pm today.
In a statement, the department said the adverse weather is forecast to affect the whole of Kelantan and Perlis, as well as Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Star, Baling, Sik, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, and Pendang in Kedah, and Hulu Perak in Perak.
Similar weather conditions are expected in Besut and Setiu in Terengganu; Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Pekan, and Rompin in Pahang; Hulu Selangor, Gombak, and Hulu Langat in Selangor; Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Kuala Pilah, and Rembau in Negri Sembilan; and Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah in Melaka.
In Sabah, the affected areas include the West Coast, the Interior (Tambunan, Keningau, Sook, Pensiangan, Membakut, and Tenom), Sandakan (Tongod, Telupid, and Paitan), and Kudat (Kota Marudu and Pitas).

Title: [UPDATED] Three students killed in Philippine school shooting, including gunman
Article:
MANILA: Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.
Eight others were injured, with four in critical condition, and all the victims were students aged 14 to 17, said Albert Palencia, mayor of Banga town in South Cotabato, where the shooting took place.
The incident follows two fatal gun incidents since June at schools in the Philippines, where school shootings were previously rare.
"The suspect supposedly sat beside his friends and told them to go home 'because after lunch, I will be executing my plan'. His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker," Palencia told Reuters.
"After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit 10 students before killing himself," Palencia added.
Last month, a student live-streamed himself shooting and killing another student in a classroom in Zamboanga in the country's south before taking ‌his own life.
In June, at least three students were killed and about 20 others injured in an attack at a public high school in Tacloban, where two classmates opened fire on campus.
The Philippines has relatively strict gun ownership regulations, including background checks and psychological evaluation requirements, although illegal firearms remain in circulation.
The Friday shooting also follows a high-profile incident in Thailand in August, where a student went on a shooting rampage at a school on the outskirts of the capital Bangkok.
South Cotabato governor Reynaldo Tamayo urged parents to ensure guns were kept out of reach of minors.
"We need to be responsible in storing firearms. Gun owners, in particular, must make sure that minors do not have access to them," Tamayo told Reuters by phone.
"We cannot expect a handful of security personnel to monitor thousands of students. We need to work together because otherwise this will be very difficult for us to address."

Title: Segamat records highest haze reading in Johor at 161, three others unhealthy
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Haze worsened across Johor today, with four of the state's eight air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings, led by Segamat at 161.
The other unhealthy readings were recorded in Tangkak (158), Batu Pahat (154) and Kluang (152). Fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less was recorded at all eight monitoring stations.
Fine particulate matter can penetrate deep into the lungs and was the main pollutant recorded at all stations.
The remaining four stations recorded moderate readings – Larkin (97), Pasir Gudang (84), Pengerang (78) and Kota Tinggi (69).
Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon urged the public to limit outdoor activities and avoid strenuous exercise in open areas.
He said children, senior citizens and those with respiratory problems should take extra precautions and, where possible, remain indoors.
Those who needed to go outside were advised to wear suitable masks, stay hydrated and seek medical attention if they developed symptoms such as coughing, breathing difficulties or irritation of the eyes and throat.
Ling also urged the public to refrain from open burning, warning that it could further worsen the haze.

Title: Tuanku Muhriz attends Friday prayers, receives memorandum of support
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir attended Friday prayers at the Tuanku Munawir Royal Mosque in Seri Menanti today, making his first public appearance after returning from abroad.
He was accompanied by his two sons, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin.
Tuanku Muhriz arrived at 1.05pm and was received by members of the mosque committee, including its imam, Abdul Rahman Ibrahim.
After Friday prayers, Tuanku Muhriz and his two sons presented contributions to children, an act that has become customary when the ruler attends Friday prayers with the people.
He then met members of the congregation in the mosque foyer before receiving a memorandum from the head of the Secretariat for Loyalty and Support to His Royal Highness the 11th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Prof Dr Mohd Aluwi Sari.
"Thank you... thank you," the ruler said briefly.
Also present were state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad.
Tuanku Muhriz left at 2.10pm.
The ruler and his sons regularly attend Friday prayers with the people in each of the Luak Tanah Mengandung as part of their routine, providing an opportunity to meet and engage with the public.
Today's development comes amid attention over Tuanku Muhriz's position as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan following a disputed proclamation.
Yesterday, Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim
confirmed
that the proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan had been approved.
He said the decision was unanimously endorsed by all members of the state executive council at its meeting on Tuesday, and that the state secretary had been instructed to proceed with its gazettement in accordance with existing regulations.
The state government said the proclamation and the appointment of Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar were valid under the state constitution.
However, the DKU maintains that Tuanku Muhriz remains the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar and that the April 19 proclamation was defective from the outset.
The DKU also disputed the status of several Undang involved in the proclamation.
Separately, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) said the menteri besar and state executive council do not have the unilateral power to remove or vacate the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The AGC said the
proclamation was invalid
as it did not comply with the mandatory requirements of Article 10 of the state Constitution, particularly as there was no evidence that any of the disqualifying grounds under Article 10(1) applied to Tuanku Muhriz.
The
state secretary's office
has since said that it would not take any action to gazette or enforce the proclamation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas: Najib can continue contributing ideas, experience under house arrest [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak can continue contributing his ideas, views and experience to the country while serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, Pas said.
Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party also expressed its gratitude to Allah and conveyed its appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting Najib a conditional pardon.
Under the pardon, Najib will serve the
remainder of his sentence
under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
"Pas prays that Datuk Seri Mohd Najib will continue to be blessed with good health while serving the remainder of his sentence at home and believes that he can still contribute his ideas, views and experience for the good of the country," he said in a statement today.
Takiyuddin said the development was significant not only to Najib's family but also to Malaysians who continued to remember and appreciate his contributions as a leader who had brought development and prosperity to the country.
"Pas conveys its highest gratitude to Allah and expresses its appreciation to His Majesty the Sultan Ibrahim for His Majesty's gracious consent to grant a conditional pardon to Datuk Seri Najib Razak," he said.
Earlier, the former Pekan MP was granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department said Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Failure to comply with any of the conditions would result in the conditional pardon being revoked and Najib having to serve the remainder of his sentence in prison.
Najib, 73, had been serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the
Federal Territories Pardons Board halved
his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.
The initial RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
Najib began serving his prison sentence after the Federal Court, on Aug 23, 2022, upheld his conviction in the SRC International corruption case.
The Pardons Board had deferred Najib's pardon application at its meeting on Sept 11, chaired by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. The decision was subsequently made at the board's 64th meeting today.

Title: Indonesian teen held after RM1.29mil Kluang drug stash house raided
Article:
JOHOR BARU: An 18-year-old Indonesian teenager was arrested after police busted a drug stash house in Kluang, seizing 25.95kg of drugs worth about RM1.29 million.
The teenager, who had overstayed in Malaysia, was arrested during the raid on a rented terrace house in Jalan Delima, Taman Lian Seng, Kluang, on Sept 13.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the house, which was rented without a tenancy agreement, was believed to have been used as a stash house by a drug trafficking syndicate.
"Police seized 25.95kg of drugs estimated to be worth RM1.29 million.
"The haul comprised eight packets of methamphetamine weighing 8.11kg and 38 packets of heroin weighing 17.84kg," he told a press conference at the Johor police contingent headquarters.
Rahaman said the suspect was believed to have been tasked with guarding the stash house, while the syndicate's mastermind remained at large.
"The syndicate is believed to have been active since January, using houses as storage facilities before distributing the drugs to the local market," he said.
The suspect had entered Malaysia legally using a passport but checks showed that he had since overstayed.
He tested negative for drugs and had no previous criminal record.
The suspect was remanded for seven days until Sunday to facilitate investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two Malaysians arrested over 10kg cannabis seizure in Singapore
Article:
SINGAPORE: Two Malaysians were arrested at Singapore's Tuas Checkpoint for attempting to smuggle more than 10kg of cannabis worth over S$203,000 (S$1=RM3.20) into the republic by hiding the drugs in their motorcycle.
The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said the 36-year-old man and 35-year-old woman were stopped upon arriving at the checkpoint on Sept 15 on a Malaysia-registered motorcycle following information received from the ICA's Integrated Targeting Centre.
In the course of the checks, ICA officers uncovered four bundles of vegetable matter believed to be controlled drugs underneath the motorcycle seat.
Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) officers were alerted and further checks uncovered six more bundles of vegetable matter believed to be controlled drugs in a black haversack on the motorcycle handlebar, ICA said in a statement.
"The seized bundles contained a total of about 10,164g of cannabis, which could potentially feed the addiction of about 1,450 abusers for a week.
"Investigations are ongoing," said ICA.
Under Section 7 of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1973, those who import into or export from Singapore more than 500g of cannabis may face the death penalty.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB to bear RM120mil-RM150mil AFA charge differentials between Sept and Dec 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) says it will bear an additional cost of RM120 million to RM150 million between Sept and Dec 2026 in automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) surcharge foregone to more than eight million domestic users who use electricity between 600kWh and 800kWh.
This comes as the government decided to increase the "safety quota" for domestic usage to 800kWh a month, which will not be charged with AFA surcharges, retail charge and service tax, from 600kWh a month.
The decision to increase the safety quota comes following complaints by certain members of the public that their electricity bills had increased drastically.
"We look forward to this [increase of the safety quota] as it gives an immediate impact to the livelihood of the people," said Datuk Shamsul Ahmad, president and group CEO of TNB.
More to come

Title: Johan Setia records highest unhealthy API reading at 192
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality at 34 stations nationwide remained unhealthy, with Johan Setia recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 192 as at 2pm today.
According to the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 32 other stations recorded moderate air quality.
Nilai, Negri Sembilan, recorded an API reading of 179, followed by Kuching, Sarawak, at 178.
Putrajaya recorded 175, while Seri Manjung, Perak, recorded 173.
Both Shah Alam and Samarahan recorded an API reading of 171, while Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 169.
Cheras and Seremban recorded 168 each, followed closely by district police headquarters Serian, Sarawak, at 167 and Tasek Ipoh, Perak, at 166.
Petaling Jaya and Banting in Selangor recorded the same reading as Sibu, Sarawak, at 165.
Klang and Alor Gajah in Melaka recorded a reading of 162, followed by Segamat, Johor, at 161.
Both Bintulu and Sarikei in Sarawak recorded 160 each.
This was followed by Bukit Rambai, Melaka, at 159 and Tangkak, Johor, at 158.
Port Dickson recorded an API reading of 156, followed by Batu Pahat, Johor, at 154.
Tanjung Malim in Perak, Temerloh, Pahang, and Sri Aman, Sarawak, recorded 153 each, while Kluang, Johor, Mukah and Kapit in Sarawak recorded a reading of 152.
At the lower end of the unhealthy air quality range, Bandaraya Melaka recorded a reading of 144, followed by Pegoh Ipoh, Perak, (140), Kuala Selangor and Jerantut, Pahang, at 134.
Meanwhile, Sandakan, Sabah, and Langkawi, Kedah, recorded good air quality, with API readings of 49 and 44, respectively.

Title: Almost 13,000 patients on organ transplant waiting list as of July
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 12,575 patients were on the organ transplant waiting list as of July, with kidney patients making up the vast majority.
The Health Ministry, through the National Transplant Centre (NTC), said 12,228 adults and 307 children were waiting for kidney transplants, followed by liver (16 patients), heart (14), lungs (three), and heart and lung (seven).
"For kidneys, the estimated waiting period is between five and 23 years, based on data from the National Renal Registry.
"Meanwhile, the waiting period for liver transplants ranges from two months to two years, based on data from the Hepatology and Gastroenterology Department at Selayang Hospital.
"For heart and lung transplants, the waiting period ranges from four months to 3.8 years, based on data from the National Heart Institute (IJN)," it said in a statement.
It said 235 organs were recovered from donors as of July, comprising kidneys, livers, hearts, lungs, corneas, bones, heart valves and skin.
"Of this number, the highest number of organs recovered were corneas (126), followed by kidneys (58), bones (24), livers (14), heart valves (10), and one each involving the heart, lungs and skin.
"Meanwhile, 436,542 people had pledged to donate their organs as of July," it said.
The ministry said organ donation can be divided into two main categories — living donation and donation after death.
"The types of organs that can be donated vary according to the donor's condition. If the donor is alive, the organs that can be donated are limited to one kidney or part of the liver.
"This is because a person can still live with one healthy kidney, while the liver has the ability to recover and regenerate after part of it is donated," it said.
However, it said living donation could only be carried out after the donor had undergone a comprehensive medical assessment to ensure the procedure was safe for the donor and suitable for the recipient.
"For individuals certified as brain dead, several organs may be considered for donation, including the kidneys, heart and lungs, as well as several types of tissue such as corneas, bones, skin and heart valves.
"However, not all organs or tissues from a donor can necessarily be used," it said.
It said every donation would be carefully assessed by a medical team based on the condition and function of the organs, the donor's medical history and suitability for potential recipients.
"Only organs and tissues deemed suitable and in good condition will be retrieved for transplantation.
"Organ donation gives patients suffering from end-stage organ failure an opportunity to receive potentially life-saving treatment.
"Meanwhile, tissue donation can help improve the quality of life of recipients," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan-Malaysia energy ties put under the spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Nearly 200 business leaders, policymakers and industry experts gathered here on Tuesday to explore ways to strengthen regional energy security through closer Japan-Malaysia cooperation.
The discussions at MUFG Net Zero World Malaysia 2026 also focused on accelerating the deployment of transition technologies and mobilising financing for commercially viable projects.
The forum focused on strengthening the Japan-Malaysia energy and industrial corridor, developing Malaysia's future energy ecosystem and making energy security bankable through transition finance.
Topics included carbon capture and storage, hydrogen, renewable energy, sustainable aviation fuel, power infrastructure and transition finance, with an emphasis on moving projects from discussion to implementation.
Japanese ambassador to Malaysia Noriyuki Shikata said Japan's technology and capital were increasingly flowing into Malaysia across strategic sectors.
"Japan's advanced technology and capital are actively flowing into Malaysia through proactive investments in AI, semiconductors, supply chain resilience, and green transformation, as well as in almost all of the 17 strategic sectors identified by the country as crucial for its growth," he said in a statement.
"This is clear evidence of the qualitative and quantitative expansion of our economic ties and presents a bright outlook for the future."
Malaysian Investment Development Authority deputy chief executive officer Zuaida Abdullah said the energy transition was reshaping economic competitiveness and investment priorities.
"The global energy transition is reshaping economic competitiveness and investment priorities.
"Building on decades of partnership, Malaysia and Japan can leverage technology and green industries to strengthen our industrial capabilities, directly supporting the New Industrial Master Plan 2030, National Energy Transition Roadmap, and Green Investment Strategy," she said.
Motohide Okuda, MUFG Malaysia's chief executive officer and country head, said progress would depend on converting discussions into actual projects.
"The opportunities ahead are significant, but real progress will depend on our ability to move from discussion to implementation," he said.
"MUFG is committed to connecting stakeholders, mobilising capital and supporting strategic partnerships that can transform promising ideas into investable projects.
"By working together, we can strengthen energy security, advance the transition journey and support sustainable economic growth across the region."
Speakers included representatives from major energy companies and experts from the Institute of Energy Economics Japan, Asian Development Bank and Japan Bank for International Cooperation.
MUFG has operated in Malaysia since 1957 and will mark 70 years in the market in 2027.
Its activities have included supporting Japanese companies expanding into Malaysia and connecting Malaysian clients to opportunities across Japan, Asean and its global network.
The bank offers conventional and Islamic banking services, having established an Islamic banking arm in 2008 - the first Japanese bank to do so in Malaysia - and contributed to the world's first yen-denominated sukuk.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KYM ventures into healthcare with RM33.5mil Regen deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KYM Holdings Bhd is proposing to acquire a 70 per cent stake in specialist healthcare provider Regen Healthcare Sdn Bhd for a maximum consideration of RM33.5 million, marking its entry into Malaysia's healthcare sector.
The proposed acquisition will diversify KYM's principal activities to include healthcare and specialised medical services, reducing its reliance on manufacturing.
Regen provides specialist healthcare services, primarily orthopaedic and ambulatory care and operates facilities.
This includes a digital hybrid operating theatre, day-care beds and multidisciplinary services covering physical rehabilitation, paediatric dentistry and special-care dentistry.
A substantial portion of the purchase consideration will be deferred and linked to Regen meeting agreed profit milestones for the financial years ending Dec 31, 2026 and 2027.
Regen founder and medical director Associate Prof Dr Rajesh Singh will retain the remaining 30 per cent stake and continue to be involved in the business.
KYM executive chairman Lim Tze Thean said the transaction followed several years of strengthening the group's financial position.
"The proposed acquisition gives KYM an opportunity to diversify its earnings base through an established operating business in a sector supported by long-term demand," he said.
Chief executive officer Darren Lee said the investment reflected four years of preparation, beginning with strengthening the balance sheet before identifying a suitable growth platform.
The acquisition and proposed diversification remain subject to relevant conditions precedent and approval by KYM shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen loses RM1 mil lawsuit over chair prank injuries
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A teenage girl who was injured after a friend pulled away the chair she was about to sit on, has lost her RM1 million lawsuit against three teachers, a headmistress, the Education Ministry and the government at the High Court.
The 14-year-old filed the suit together with her father, Wan Amey Shahril Wan Ab Rahman, 39, as the first and second plaintiffs, respectively.
They named three teachers, Ilyana Sari Ridzuan, Suhaida Abdul Rahman and Aizam Naim Mohd Junid; headmistress Hamidah Shamsudin; the ministry and the government as the first to sixth defendants, respectively, alleging negligence that resulted in the girl's injuries.
In delivering her judgment, Judicial Commissioner Datuk Anita Harun said the first plaintiff, who was 11 at the time of the incident, fell fractured her left femur while attending a special education programme at a national school here on Oct 12, 2023.
"The plaintiffs alleged negligence and a breach of the duty of care owed to the student.
"Teachers have a duty to ensure the safety of students, as provided for under the law.
"However, this duty does not mean that teachers can guarantee that students will never be injured," she said.
She said the plaintiffs still had to prove, on the balance of probabilities, that the teachers' negligence had caused the loss or injury.
Anita said the first plaintiff's claim that the incident happened due to a lack of supervision when she fell, resulting in injury, was not proven.
"The first plaintiff herself acknowledged that the incident happened quickly and without any prior argument. The alleged failure of supervision and the cause of the fall could not be established," she said.
She said that based on the chronology of the case, the medical history placed the time of the incident at about 10am, while the victim's mother, Azera Yazid, 38, estimated that it occurred at 10.40am and that she arrived at the school at about 11.20am.
"The court also accepted evidence that the victim received assistance, cried and then moved towards her father on the lower floor of the school building.
"The school's procedures supported contacting the parents, but did not require an ambulance to be called.
"Considering the assistance provided, the prompt arrival of the victim's mother, the teachers' observations and the passage of time, arranging for the parents to collect her rather than providing emergency transportation was reasonable in the circumstances.
"The child should have remained resting and received appropriate assistance when moving towards her father," she said.
Anita said no separate administrative failure that caused the loss could be established, while the necessary basis for determining liability also failed to be proven on the balance of probabilities.
"The plaintiffs' action against all the defendants is dismissed," she said.
During the proceedings, all the defendants were represented by senior federal counsel Afiq Nazrin Zaharinan, while both plaintiffs were represented by lawyer Soffian Azmir.
On Aug 4, 2024, it was reported that the girl, who was then 12, had suffered for almost a year from complications arising from a spinal injury after falling when a
schoolmate pulled away the chair
she was about to sit on.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former jewellery supervisor jailed 16 months over RM176,200 gold theft
Article:
Pix by Fathil Asri
KUALA LUMPUR: A former jewellery store supervisor was sentenced to 16 months in jail and three strokes of the rotan after pleading guilty to three charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM176,200 worth of gold bars.
Koh Mun Hoe, 33, had taken three gold bars weighing 250 grammes from his employer's vault, pawned them and invested the proceeds in cryptocurrency, suffering losses of about RM235,000.
The store manager conducted a stock check on June 16 and discovered that three gold bars — one weighing 50 grammes and two weighing 100 grammes each — were missing from the vault.
Closed-circuit television recordings showed Koh taking the gold bars from the vault without his employer's authorisation on June 4, 6 and 8 at the premises in a shopping mall in Cheras.
Questioned by the company, Koh admitted taking the gold bars on the three occasions and concealing them in his vest pocket before walking out of the premises.
He then pawned the gold bars and used the money to trade in cryptocurrency, but suffered losses of about RM235,000.
Koh was arrested at 1am on June 17 at the Cheras police district headquarters Commercial Crime Investigation Department.
Sessions Court judge Azrul Darus imposed the sentence after Koh pleaded guilty to three charges of criminal breach of trust.
The charges, framed under Section 408 of the Penal Code, relate to Koh dishonestly using property entrusted to him for his own benefit by pawning the gold bars.
The offence carries a jail term of between one and 14 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Handcuffed in the dock, Koh pleaded for leniency, telling the court that he was recently divorced and was supporting his two children, aged six and three, as well as his elderly parents.
"I made a mistake and a wrong decision, and I was ill-advised about the investment.
"I hope to receive a lesser jail sentence and that the court will give me a chance to repent so that I can return to my family and support them.
"This is my first offence and I will not do it again," he said, as his uncle watched the proceedings from the public gallery.
Koh is also facing a fourth CBT charge before another Sessions Court involving an 80-gramme gold chain worth RM57,840.82, which he allegedly took as his own before pawning it.
He allegedly committed the offence on June 12 at the same premises.
Judge Dr Azrol Abdullah fixed Sept 22 for sentencing. Deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Ikhwan Mohd Nasir prosecuted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three held as police bust drug stash houses in Senai, seize pistol, RM51,000
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A drug syndicate that allegedly turned two illegally built houses in Senai into stash houses was busted with the arrest of three suspects, including an 18-year-old woman believed to have managed its finances.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspects were detained in two raids at adjoining houses in Kampung Sepakat Baru, Kulai, at 6pm on Sept 11.
In the first raid, police arrested two men, one believed to be the syndicate's drug dealer and the other his accomplice.
"Police seized a Czech-made CZ pistol and 79 rounds of 9mm ammunition.
"Police confiscated suspected contraband, including 72g of methamphetamine, 5g of heroin, 42 yaba pills and 57g of cannabis.
"Also seized were 4.6kg of caffeine packed in 10 plastic packets, believed to be used as a cutting agent to dilute or bulk up the drugs for distribution," Rahaman told a press conference at the Johor police contingent headquarters today.
In the second raid at the adjoining house, police arrested the 18-year-old woman, who is believed to have acted as the syndicate's financial manager.
Police seized another 75g of methamphetamine and 10g of heroin from the house.
Rahaman said the total drug haul weighed 278g and was estimated to be worth RM11,401.
Police also seized a Mercedes C180, a lorry, two motorcycles, RM51,000 and jewellery worth RM22,788.
He said preliminary checks found that the pistol appeared to be a genuine firearm, with a functionality test pending.
"Checks so far found no record linking the pistol to any previous criminal activity.
"We believe the syndicate had been active since June, using rented houses without tenancy agreements as drug storage facilities before distributing the drugs to the local market," he said.
Urine screening also found both male suspects positive for morphine, while checks revealed previous drug-related records involving two of the suspects.
All three suspects have been remanded until Sept 21 to facilitate investigations under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952 and Section 8 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Media camp outside Najib's residence following conditional house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Local and international media personnel have gathered outside the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak in Jalan Duta here today, following a decision allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
More than 50 media practitioners were seen at the scene to cover the latest developments following the conditional pardon.
As of 2pm, there had been no movement in or out of Najib's residence.
The situation remained under control, with no supporters of the former Pekan member of parliament seen at the location. Several police vehicles were also stationed nearby for security purposes.
Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board said Najib had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.
The board said
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
It added that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed under the pardon, failing which the conditional pardon could be revoked.
Najib, 73, is currently serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the Pardons Board reduced his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.
The board also reduced the RM210 million fine imposed on him to RM50 million.
Najib began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and sentence in the SRC International case.
He was found guilty of seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering over RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former unit of 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).
He was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.
Najib subsequently submitted a petition for a royal pardon.
The Pardons Board met in January 2024 and announced the reduction of his prison term to six years and his fine to RM50 million.
Under that decision, his release date was set for Aug 23, 2028, while failure to pay the RM50 million fine would have resulted in an additional year in prison, extending the release date to Aug 23, 2029.
The latest decision maintains Aug 23, 2028 as the end date of his sentence, while allowing him to serve the remainder under house arrest, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with the conditions of the conditional pardon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says constitutional process must be followed in Negri Sembilan
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed the need for the Negri Sembilan government to adhere strictly to constitutional provisions and established procedures in dealing with the dispute over the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
He said the removal of a ruler was not a trivial matter and that any action involving the institution of the monarchy must comply fully with the Constitution.
"Our country is founded on a constitutional system and upholds the institution of the monarchy. If this matter is made light of, it will create many problems.
"I do not reject the legal principles applicable in Negri Sembilan or the Adat concerning the system of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and the Undangs.
"But we must ensure that the rules are fully complied with and that the proper procedures are followed.
"What is important for us at this point is that the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar is not affected.
"We pray to Allah that His Highness will be able to 'bersemayam' and carry out his duties well," he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Surau Nur Perdana in Presint 10 here.
He added that Malays, in particular, should set a good example by upholding the Constitution and preserving harmony.
"If there is any proposal from the Undangs or others, the process and rules must be followed fully. These rules do not apply only to the Ruler, but also to the Undangs.
"Follow the process, and we should not interfere beyond that."
His remarks came amid a dispute over an
April 19 proclamation
purporting to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan.
The state government had maintained that the proclamation and the appointment of Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar were valid under the state Constitution.
However, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) Negri Sembilan maintained that Tuanku Muhriz remained the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar and disputed the validity of the proclamation.
The DKU also disputed the status of several Undang involved in the proclamation.
The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) subsequently said the Menteri Besar and state
executive council did not
have unilateral power to remove or vacate the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The A-GC said the validity and legal effect of the April 19 proclamation must be determined through the constitutional and legal process under the Negri Sembilan Constitution.
It said the proclamation was invalid as it did not comply with the mandatory requirements of Article 10 of the state Constitution, particularly as there was no evidence that any of the disqualifying grounds under Article 10(1) applied to Tuanku Muhriz.
While the Datuk-Datuk Undang have the power to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, the A-GC said Article 10 also sets out the procedures and grounds that must be considered before such a decision can be made.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three men fined RM4,500 each for assisting unlicensed moneylender
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Three men were each fined RM4,500 by the magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to charges linked to unlicensed moneylending.
The three — Kelvin Tee, 24, Ng Yong Siong, 25, and Gavin Kho, 24 — were charged under Section 29AA of the Moneylenders Act 1951 for assisting an unlicensed moneylender.
They pleaded guilty to three separate charges before the court.
The court fined each of them RM4,500, in default of three months' imprisonment. All three paid their fines.
The men were arrested following a police report lodged at the Nusa Bestari police station on Sept 15 concerning unlicensed moneylending activities.
The case was investigated under Section 5(2) of the Moneylenders Act 1951 for operating an unlicensed moneylending business.
